advances: This turns one affine choice of actual metronoid points on finitely many integer fibers into an admissible complete-core tuple of the same total mass. In proper base rank it gives the relative capacity required by the convex-filling branch, and in full base rank it gives the global capacity. The construction remains valid when the chosen fibers span a lower-dimensional affine subspace of the prescribed base subspace.
author: research-agent
proof:
Let \(L_0:=\operatorname{aff}E\) and \(r:=\dim L_0\), so \(0\le r\le q\). We first construct a centerpoint intrinsically in \(L_0\), rather than assuming that \(E\) spans \(L\).

Fix \(y_0\in E\), and let \(V_0:=L_0-y_0\). Because \(V_0\) is spanned over \(\mathbb R\) by the integer vectors \(y-y_0\), \(y\in E\), the group \(\Gamma_0:=V_0\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is a rank-\(r\) lattice spanning \(V_0\). Choose a lattice basis of \(\Gamma_0\). It defines an affine isomorphism

\[
\psi:L_0\longrightarrow\mathbb R^r
\quad\text{with}\quad
\psi(L_0\cap\mathbb Z^n)=\mathbb Z^r.
\]

Consider the nonzero finite Borel measure

\[
\widetilde\mu:=\sum_{y\in E}t_y\,\delta_{\psi(y)}
\]

on \(\mathbb R^r\). It has total mass \(T>0\) and is supported on \(\mathbb Z^r\). Apply accepted fact 6d6fcf377e68c79c with discrete dimension \(r\) and continuous dimension zero. It gives \(u\in\mathbb Z^r\) such that every closed halfspace of \(\mathbb R^r\) containing \(u\) has \(\widetilde\mu\)-mass at least \(2^{-r}T\).

If \(r>0\) and \(u\notin\operatorname{conv}\psi(E)\), strict separation from the compact convex set \(\operatorname{conv}\psi(E)\) would give a proper closed halfspace containing \(u\) and disjoint from \(\psi(E)\). Its \(\widetilde\mu\)-mass would be zero, contradicting \(2^{-r}T>0\). If \(r=0\), both \(\mathbb R^r\) and \(\operatorname{conv}\psi(E)\) consist of their unique point. Hence in every case \(u\in\operatorname{conv}\psi(E)\). Set

\[
m:=\psi^{-1}(u).
\]

Then \(m\in L_0\cap\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}E\), so in particular \(m\in L\cap\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}E\), and \(\Lambda_m(E)\ne\varnothing\).

Let \(J_L\subseteq L\) be a proper relative closed halfspace containing \(m\). Its trace on \(L_0\) contains \(m\). If the defining affine functional is constant on \(L_0\), then \(J_L\cap L_0=L_0\), and therefore

\[
\sum_{y\in E\cap J_L}t_y=T.
\]

Otherwise \(\psi(J_L\cap L_0)\) is a proper closed halfspace of \(\mathbb R^r\) containing \(u\), so the centerpoint property gives

\[
\sum_{y\in E\cap J_L}t_y
=\widetilde\mu\bigl(\psi(J_L\cap L_0)\bigr)
\ge 2^{-r}T
\ge 2^{-q}T.
\]

The constant-restriction case satisfies the same final bound. This proves the required relative \(2^{-q}\) balance even when \(r<q\). When \(q=0\), also \(r=0\), the set \(E\) is a singleton and there are no proper relative closed halfspaces of \(L\), so the same conclusion is valid without an omitted boundary case.

It remains to construct a point in every required Minkowski sum. Define

\[
p:=s(m).
\]

For any \(\lambda\in\Lambda_m(E)\), affineness of \(s\) and the defining equations for \(\Lambda_m(E)\) give

\[
p=s\!\left(\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y y\right)
=\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y s(y).
\]

Since \(s(y)\in\mathsf M_{t_y}(C_y)\) for every \(y\in E\), this equality implies

\[
p\in\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y\mathsf M_{t_y}(C_y).
\]

This is the same point \(p\) for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_m(E)\); zero coefficients use the standard convention \(0Q=\{0\}\). Thus

\[
p\in\mathcal K_m(\mathsf M_t),
\qquad
\mathcal K_m(\mathsf M_t)\ne\varnothing.
\]

Because \(t_y>0\) and \(t_y\le a_y\), every \(y\in E\) lies in \(I_+\). If \(q<n\), the tuple \((E,(t_y)_{y\in E},m)\) therefore satisfies every condition in the definition of \(G_L^{\mathrm{rel}}\) in accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb: positive feasible fiber masses, an integral centerpoint in \(\operatorname{conv}E\), relative \(2^{-q}\) halfspace balance, and a nonempty complete metronoid core. Its total mass is \(T\), so \(G_L^{\mathrm{rel}}\ge T\).

If \(q=n\), the full-dimensional affine subspace \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) equals \(\mathbb R^n\). Its proper relative closed halfspaces are exactly the proper closed halfspaces of \(\mathbb R^n\). The same tuple is therefore admissible in the global definition of \(G\) in accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb, with balance \(2^{-n}\), and \(G\ge T\). This proves both conclusions.
statement:
Use the mixed convex-body setup and the canonical notation of accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb: \(C_y:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(y,x)\in C\}\), \(a_y:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_y)\), and \(I_+:=\{y\in\mathbb Z^n:a_y>0\}\). For \(0<t\le a_y\), let \(\mathsf M_t(C_y)\) be the metronoid defined there. For finite nonempty \(E\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) and \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}E\), write

\[
\Lambda_m(E):=
\left\{
\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^E:
\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y=1,
\quad
\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y y=m
\right\}
\]

and

\[
\mathcal K_m(\mathsf M_t):=
\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda_m(E)}
\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y\mathsf M_{t_y}(C_y).
\]

Let \(L=b+V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a primitive affine lattice subspace of rank \(q\), meaning that \(b\in\mathbb Z^n\), \(\dim V=q\), and \(V\cap\mathbb Z^n\) is a saturated rank-\(q\) lattice. Assume \(0\le q\le n\). Let \(E\subseteq L\cap\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and nonempty, let \(0<t_y\le a_y\) for every \(y\in E\), and suppose that an affine map \(s:L\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfies

\[
s(y)\in\mathsf M_{t_y}(C_y)
\qquad(y\in E).
\]

Put \(T:=\sum_{y\in E}t_y\). There exist an integer point \(m\in L\cap\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}E\) and a point \(p\in\mathbb R^d\) such that

\[
\sum_{y\in E\cap J_L}t_y\ge 2^{-q}T
\]

for every proper relative closed halfspace \(J_L\subseteq L\) containing \(m\), and

\[
p\in
\sum_{y\in E}\lambda_y\mathsf M_{t_y}(C_y)
\qquad
\text{for every }\lambda\in\Lambda_m(E).
\]

Consequently, if \(q<n\), then the relative complete metronoid-core capacity from accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb satisfies

\[
G_L^{\mathrm{rel}}\ge T.
\]

If \(q=n\), then necessarily \(L=\mathbb R^n\), and the global complete metronoid-core capacity satisfies

\[
G\ge T.
\]
